title: Transfer Learning & Fine-tuning in Vision
interviewAnswer: Transfer learning starts from pretrained visual features and adapts them to a target task. With limited data, freeze more layers initially; with enough domain data, fine-tune carefully using smaller learning rates and validation.
keyPoints: Head-only training is a baseline, not a law.
why: Transfer Learning & Fine-tuning in Vision is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: Transfer learning starts from pretrained visual features and adapts them to a target task. With limited data, freeze more layers initially; with enough domain data, fine-tune carefully using smaller learning rates and validation. Head-only training is a baseline, not a law. Catastrophic forgetting/overfitting can occur. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Fine-tune a pretrained ResNet on a small industrial defect dataset and compare with training from scratch.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Transfer Learning & Fine-tuning in Vision?
How would you validate or tune Transfer Learning & Fine-tuning in Vision?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
